briefings.title: AI, Infrastructure, and the Next Investment Cycle
briefings.tldr: Driven heavily by tech (which accounts for ~55% of US capital spending and nearly 40% of aggregate stock market value), current market highs are supported by fundamental earnings rather than multiple expansion.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Driven heavily by tech (which accounts for ~55% of US capital spending and nearly 40% of aggregate stock market value), current market highs are supported by fundamental earnings rather than multiple expansion. Meanwhile, AI infrastructure buildout and agentic workflows are accelerating demand across compute, power, and physical supply chains.

## Macro, Markets, and the Infrastructure Boom
* **High-Tech Capital Concentration:**
  * High-tech equipment, software, and R&D account for roughly 55% of US capital spending (**David George**).
  * US tech companies represent 8 of the top 10 valued companies globally, with tech comprising almost 40% of the aggregate US stock market value (**David George**).
  * Model companies combined have raised over $350 billion (**David George**).
* **Earnings-Driven Market Highs:**
  * The market is up 90% (17% annualized) since JBT came out almost 4 years ago (**Alex Immerman**, **David George**).
  * Stocks are up ~20% while trading multiples are down ~20%, meaning performance is driven by fundamental earnings rather than multiple expansion (**David George**).
  * The S&P 500 earnings multiple is below 20x, while cyclical memory companies trade at 6x–7x forward earnings (**David George**).
* **Massive Hyperscaler CapEx & Infrastructure Scale:**
  * The AI infrastructure buildout has surpassed railroads as a percentage of GDP (**David George**).
  * CapEx for the five largest hyperscalers (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle) is projected at $416 billion in 2025, $780 billion in 2026, and over $1 trillion annually from 2027 onward (**David George**).
  * Combined cloud backlog for Microsoft, Google, and Amazon sits at roughly $1.7 trillion (**David George**).
* **The "Age of Atoms" & Power Grids:**
  * Global infrastructure investment needs are estimated at $90 trillion through 2040 across power, water, roads, transit, and manufacturing (**Santiago Rodriguez**).
  * Portfolio examples include Anduril’s manufacturing facility (spanning 87 football fields), Waymo depot expansions, and SpaceX's $100 billion investment in Louisiana (**Santiago Rodriguez**).
  * Data centers can actually help lower residential electricity rates; a US study showed that for every 10% increase in data center capacity, residential electricity rates decreased by 40 basis points due to spreading fixed grid costs over more units of electricity (**Santiago Rodriguez**, **Alex Immerman**).

## Models, Applications, and Enterprise Adoption
* **Rapid Revenue Growth at the Model Layer:**
  * Combined annualized revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic has climbed significantly, well-surpassing net new revenue estimates for the greatest software companies in history (**Sarah Wang**).
* **Early Enterprise Diffusion:**
  * Live deployments at S&P 500 companies stand at 69%, but quantifiable impact sits at 30%, and tracked recurring impact is only at 2% (**Sarah Wang**).
  * Most enterprise exposure remains limited to Microsoft Copilot (**Sarah Wang**).
  * Forward-leaning large Fortune 500 companies allocate roughly 1% of headcount-equivalent spend to AI tools, whereas AI-native portfolio companies reach up to 10% (**David George**).
* **Power Users Pulling Away:**
  * Median AI vendor spending in the top 1% of users is roughly 8x the level of the top 10% (**Sarah Wang**).
  * In AI-native portfolio companies, top users spend $7,500 to $9,000 per month, compared to median users spending $200 to $400 monthly (**Sarah Wang**).
* **Measurable ROI and Cost Reductions:**
  * Chime reduced its cost-to-serve by over 10% annually for four years (compounding to nearly a 50% total reduction), supported by Decagon (**Alex Immerman**).
  * Shopify's AI sidekick helped increase the percentage of onboarded merchants reaching 5 orders within 15 days by 8% (**Alex Immerman**).
  * ServiceNow reported over $1 billion in AI annual contract value (ACV) and a 9x increase in agentic deployments (**Sarah Wang**).
  * Stripe's SAS customer data shows growth accelerating into 2026 across both young and mature businesses, a dynamic Stripe calls "the renaissance" (**Alex Immerman**, **Sarah Wang**).

## Agents, Costs, and Efficiency Gains
* **Plummeting Inference Costs & Agent Scaling:**
  * Agent token usage on Open Router experienced 14x growth (**Santiago Rodriguez**).
  * Context caching has drastically lowered costs (e.g., Hebia saw financial chat workloads become 10x cheaper to run) (**Santiago Rodriguez**).
  * Advanced routing (e.g., Data Bricks' smart router) solves more problems at 35% lower cost than the strongest individual model (**Sarah Wang**).
  * Fine-tuning smaller models (e.g., Elise AI fine-tuning a model to be 60% cheaper with lower latency) makes live audio use cases tenable (**Sarah Wang**).

## Consumer AI and Marketplaces
* **Consumer Adoption and Engagement:**
  * Just over 2% of US households have a paying subscription for AI (**Santiago Rodriguez**).
  * AI subscriptions exhibit "smiling retention curves" that flatline and actually rise as products improve (**Santiago Rodriguez**, **Alex Immerman**).
* **Marketplace Impact and Frictionless Commerce:**
  * While Amazon declined integration with Muse, Instacart integrated it, looking to capture incremental orders and GMV from automated agentic purchasing (**Santiago Rodriguez**).
  * Search engines like Google have remained resilient because high-monetizing ad terms (e.g., buying insurance, booking hotels) involve intent that AI has not fully automated on the user's behalf (**Alex Immerman**).

## Public and Private Software Markets
* **Public Software Biffurcation:**
  * Roughly 75% of public software companies are profitable, but only 30% are growing at 20% or more (**Sarah Wang**).
  * Cybersecurity (e.g., CrowdStrike), observability, and vertical software have held up significantly better than horizontal applications (**Sarah Wang**).
* **Late-Stage Private Champions:**
  * The top 6 private companies (Anthropic, OpenAI, Databricks, Stripe, Waymo, Revolut) have a combined last-round valuation of $2.4 trillion—larger than the combined market cap of all IPOs over the last 10 years excluding SpaceX ($1.7 trillion) (**Alex Immerman**).
* **Secondary Liquidity Dynamics:**
  * Employee participation in company-held tender offers tracked by Carta is only 58%, reflecting high employee conviction in business performance (**Alex Immerman**).
  * Discounts on secondary market transactions relative to last-round prices are essentially zero, contrasting with previous years (**Alex Immerman**).

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **CapEx Projections:** Hyperscaler CapEx will exceed $1 trillion annually starting in 2027 — **David George**
* **Cumulative Tech Investment:** Cumulative technology investment numbers will be 20x higher over the next 5 to 7, potentially 10 years — **David George**
* **Autonomous Driving Scale:** Fully autonomous driving networks (currently 14x safer than human drivers) will expand miles traveled by at least an order of magnitude, and all 17 million new cars sold annually in the US will be autonomous over the next 10 years — **David George**
* **Robotics Investment:** Robotics investment will become even larger than LLMs (though arriving 3 to 5 years earlier), driving massive investment and excitement over the next 5 years — **David George**
* **Military Hardware Diffusion:** Newer defense vendors (like Anduril, Saronic, and Castellian) will grow dramatically from their current baseline of under 5% of overall military dollars spent as needs change — **David George**

---

## Notable Quotes
> "Tech is driving the investment cycle obviously across all areas of the economy... and just to put it into into very deep historical context... this buildout just surpassed railroads as a percentage of GDP."
> — **David George**

> "AI is generating major revenue and savings. On the other hand, adoption is still extremely early."
> — **David George**

> "The AI can know a lot about the world but know very little about your company. And we're seeing this in our application layer companies where they're bridging this gap."
> — **Sarah Wang**

> "Investing in physical infrastructure is very different than investing in software. Elon coined the term 'the factory is the product' many years ago. It's no surprise that a lot of the great founders that we've backed have come out of Tesla or SpaceX."
> — **Santiago Rodriguez**

briefings.tldr: Citadel CEO Ken Griffin is committing a record $3 billion to Carnegie Mellon University—with $2 billion funding a new campus in Miami and $1 billion supporting the main Pittsburgh campus, including naming the Kenneth C. Griffin School of Computer Science—to pioneer a tech-forward, interdisciplinary model for higher education focused on return on investment and grand societal challenges.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## **TL;DR**
Citadel CEO Ken Griffin is committing a record $3 billion to Carnegie Mellon University—with $2 billion funding a new campus in Miami and $1 billion supporting the main Pittsburgh campus, including naming the Kenneth C. Griffin School of Computer Science—to pioneer a tech-forward, interdisciplinary model for higher education focused on return on investment and grand societal challenges.

## **The $3 Billion Carnegie Mellon Donation & Strategy**
* **Record-Breaking Financial Commitment:** 
  * Citadel founder Ken Griffin is making a $3 billion gift to Carnegie Mellon University (CMU), marking the largest single gift ever committed to a U.S. university and doubling his total philanthropic investments in CMU.
* **Allocation of Funds:**
  * **$2 billion** is designated to build and establish a new campus in Miami.
  * **$1 billion** goes to the main campus in Pittsburgh, which includes naming the institution's top-ranked computer science program the **Kenneth C. Griffin School of Computer Science**.
* **Institutional Rankings & ROI:** 
  * According to Ken Griffin, U.S. News rankings place CMU **number three** in the country for return on investment on a college education, propelling the school to **number 14 overall** in the U.S.

## **A New Model for Higher Education**
* **Breaking Down Silos:** 
  * According to President Farnam Jahanian, the new Miami campus and educational model will organize around grand societal challenges (such as human health, national security, cyber security, and energy/climate resiliency) rather than traditional departments, colleges, and schools.
* **Balancing Technical Rigor and the Humanities:** 
  * Ken Griffin emphasizes the need for well-rounded students who combine foundational technical and scientific knowledge with human skills like problem-solving, communication, and ethical application.
  * President Jahanian and Griffin noted CMU's deep roots in the humanities, highlighting alumni achievements including **nearly 70 Tony Award winners**, the first school of drama in the U.S. (founded in **1914**), and artist Andy Warhol.
* **Urban Re-industrialization and Economic Impact:** 
  * Pittsburgh’s economic renaissance is anchored by CMU, which currently features **100 different robotics companies** driving the re-industrialization of the U.S.
  * Griffin intends for the new CMU Miami campus to similarly transform Miami by attracting hundreds of technology companies, startups, and career opportunities.

## **Higher Education Reform and Core Mission**
* **Shifting the Campus Narrative:** 
  * Ken Griffin stated that American campuses have improved over the past **two years** (since **2024**), noting that the pendulum is shifting back to the center after universities briefly "lost the narrative" of preparing students for the workforce.
* **The Ethos of College:** 
  * Griffin criticized viewing college as "four years of fun" or "four years of an entitlement," arguing that the true ethos should be preparing young people to make a tangible difference in America.
  * President Jahanian affirmed that universities must stay true to their core mission of educating the next generation, creating knowledge to benefit society, and driving economic and cultural impact.

## **Notable Quotes**
> "This is an investment in excellence. Carnegie Melon University leads the nation in computer science, in artificial intelligence, in cyber security. Worldrenowned program robotics. This is a university that represents the future of our country." 
> — **Ken Griffin**

> "Whenever there are massive societal and technological changes, CMU steps up. We make big bold bets. And this is one of those I think given the changes that we see in technology advances we see in AI there's no question that every sector of our economy is being transformed." 
> — **Farnam Jahanian**

> "The point of higher education is to educate our young men and women to lead our country, to run businesses, to create new products, to entertain us, to actually enter the workforce and have tangible skills in solving problems." 
> — **Ken Griffin**

briefings.title: Ex-NVIDIA Engineer: Why AI Is Running Out of Copper
briefings.tldr: As AI models exceed single-GPU capacity, traditional copper interconnects are hitting physical limits, driving the industry toward optical interconnects and silicon photonics.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
As AI models exceed single-GPU capacity, traditional copper interconnects are hitting physical limits, driving the industry toward optical interconnects and silicon photonics. Thema's Herwig Van Hove and Yannick De Koninck are tackling this infrastructure bottleneck by building large-scale silicon photonics manufacturing in Europe.

## The Infrastructure Bottleneck: Why Copper is Reaching Its Limit
* **GPU-to-GPU Communication Limits:** 
  * As AI models grow too large for a single GPU, multiple GPUs must be interconnected.
  * Copper interconnects are running out of steam because modern AI workloads require higher data transfer rates and bandwidth.
* **Shift to Optical Interconnects:** 
  * The transition from copper to optical interconnects and silicon photonics is necessary to support the immense data throughput required by modern AI.
* **The AI Factory Architecture Shift:** 
  * **Network Topology:** Traditional hyper-scale data centers relied on a deep hierarchical tree of switches for Google searches. Modern AI infrastructure requires a much flatter network with direct connections between switches and GPUs to handle high-volume, latency-sensitive GPU-to-GPU traffic (including agentic AI tool calls).
* **The Energy Crisis:** 
  * **Existential Threat:** Data center energy consumption is the number one issue keeping CTOs awake at night because local power grids cannot deliver sufficient power.
  * **Grid Constraints:** Google spent three years negotiating with Amsterdam before moving plans to Belgium due to a lack of power grid capacity. Upgrading grids or building new power plants cannot keep pace with AI demand.
  * **Photonics as the Killer App:** Energy consumption is the ultimate killer app for silicon photonics, a technology 20 to 30 years in the making.

## Market Dynamics & The Supply Chain Deficit
* **Explosive Market Growth:** 
  * BlackRock's Tony Kim estimates a $10 trillion industry rebuild, with data centers being heavily impacted due to outdated, water- and energy-inefficient infrastructure.
  * NVIDIA made massive investments in 2024 and 2025, investing 4x the total market size in the first 6 months of the year into companies like Lumentum and Coherent to push the market toward photonics.
* **Supply Chain Bottlenecks:** 
  * **Component Scarcity:** While foundries (TSMC, GlobalFoundries, Tower) handle front-end silicon photonics wafers, final chips require lasers (produced by Lumentum, Coherent) and raw substrates, which face severe supply limitations.
  * **Manufacturing Challenges:** Tool builders are not producing nearly enough tools, and existing tools suffer from low throughput, efficiency, and yield.
  * **Geopolitical Divide:** The East-West divide creates additional friction in securing raw materials and substrates.

## Thema's European Manufacturing Strategy
* **Founding and Infrastructure:** 
  * Thema acquired a large-scale European foundry that went out of business, gaining ready-to-go cleanrooms and complex infrastructure that would normally take 3 to 5 years to permit and build.
  * The location is strategically positioned 20 kilometers away from IMEC (Interuniversity Microelectronics Center), a world-leading research center and birthplace of silicon photonics.
* **Talent Acquisition:** 
  * Despite initial skepticism about hiring, Thema successfully attracted top-tier talent from companies like Amazon Web Services (AWS), TSMC, Lam Research, and NVIDIA.
  * The board includes three senior figures from IMEC, including the visionary professor who founded the photonics department at the University of Gent (which produced 35% of the 4,000 peer-reviewed global photonics white papers between 2000 and 2015).
* **Overcoming Misconceptions:** 
  * American tier-one customers initially questioned Thema's ability to secure funding, talent, machines, and substrates while meeting aggressive timelines due to the stereotype that Europe is slow and committee-driven.
  * Thema is intentionally adopting a "fail fast" and agile corporate culture to counter traditional European bureaucracy.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Production Timeline:** Thema plans to start production in **2027** and work toward a full ramp-up by **2028** — *Herwig Van Hove & Yannick De Koninck*.

## Notable Quotes
> "I moved back to IMAC where I worked on laser integration for silicon photonics for a while and then five years ago I joined Nvidia back then when I still had to explain to people what Nvidia actually was."
> — Yannick De Koninck

> "Every deep tech paradigm shift needs a killer app for photonics. More than 20 years in the making, 30 years in the making in on the science side, energy consumption by data centers and AI is that killer app."
> — Herwig Van Hove

> "I realized that this was a once in a-lifetime opportunity for me to join a mission that's going to solve some of the core problems that are slowing down probably one of the biggest or the biggest technological revolution that I will witness in my lifetime. So I decided to leave the golden palace and jump onto the pirate ship and set sail."
> — Yannick De Koninck

briefings.title: Horizon Robotics CEO: Car Chips, Mind-Off Driving and China's Speed | Podcast | In Good Company
briefings.tldr: Horizon Robotics founder and CEO Dr. Kai Yu explains how his 11-year-old "Wintel"-style computing platform powers one in three intelligent vehicles in China, detailing the intense competitive market, autonomous driving timelines, and the inevitable convergence of cars and humanoid robotics.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Horizon Robotics founder and CEO Dr. Kai Yu explains how his 11-year-old "Wintel"-style computing platform powers one in three intelligent vehicles in China, detailing the intense competitive market, autonomous driving timelines, and the inevitable convergence of cars and humanoid robotics.

## Company Overview & Positioning
* **Core Business:** Dr. Kai Yu describes Horizon Robotics as the computing platform provider for generic robots, currently focused 95-100% on passenger vehicles by supplying chips and software spanning camera perception, trajectory planning, and control.
* **Market Share & Customer Base:** 
  * Supplies chips and software to **one in three** intelligent cars on Chinese roads (up from one in four previously).
  * Major Chinese original equipment manufacturer (OEM) customers include BYD, Geely, Chery, Changan, and Great Wall.
  * Global OEM customers include Volkswagen, Toyota, and Suzuki.
* **Competitive Landscape:** Competes with Mobileye, Huawei, Black Sesame, Qualcomm, MediaTek, Texas Instruments, Renesas, and NXP. Yu notes that the automotive computing space in China has consolidated around three primary players: Nvidia, Huawei, and Horizon Robotics.
* **The "Wintel" Strategy:** Deliberately chose never to build a car, instead modeling Horizon Robotics after Microsoft and Intel ("a Vintel") to enable all car brands and the broader robotics ecosystem rather than competing with them.
* **Company Scale:** Employs around **2,000 people**, the vast majority being software and hardware engineers operating under a high-ownership, flexible-hour culture.

## Market Dynamics & Supply Chain Intensity
* **China's Hyper-Competitive Car Market:** Describes the domestic market as "crazy," noting there are **60 to 70** different car brands and that more than **580 new car models** were launched in the first half of the year alone.
* **Development Cycle Discrepancy:** 
  * Initiating a new chip and solution generation takes **3 to 4 years** to ready for car makers.
  * Securing a nomination requires a production cycle of **2 years** for Chinese OEMs, compared to **5 years** for global OEMs.
  * Total cycle time spans **5 to 8 years** from start to finished platform.
* **China's Supply Chain Advantage:** Yu highlights China as a "wonderland for supply chain" due to its rich ecosystem, geographic proximity ("taking the entire China as one village"), and speed, allowing innovations to be realized rapidly through local partners.
* **The High-Barrier Paradox:** Acknowledges that automotive is "terrible business" requiring heavy investment with very slow returns, but argues that these mission-critical safety and quality standards create an extremely high entry barrier that filters out casual VC-funded newcomers.

## Autonomous Driving Timelines & Robotics Convergence
* **Three-Stage Autonomous Roadmap:** Reaffirms milestones established in January of the previous year to measure progress for consumers:
  * **Hands-off:** Target by the end of **2028** (currently enabled by the Horizon Superdrive software stack running on the Journey 6T SOC).
  * **Eyes-off:** Target by the end of **2030** (requiring larger knowledge bases, test mileage, and statistical safety proof).
  * **Minds-off:** Target by the end of **2035** (allowing passengers to sleep while the vehicle operates).
* **Robotics Convergence:** 
  * Horizon Robotics is already a top-two player in generic robotics computing in China, supplying chip solutions to humanoid robot companies.
  * Yu predicts that car technology and humanoid robotics will eventually converge into a unifying computing platform because cars fundamentally function as moving robots.
  * Foresees meaningful volumes of humanoid robots in home service and elderly care within **5 years** (optimistic projection).
  * Argues that winning the automotive supply chain directly translates to winning the robotics supply chain due to shared actuators and sensors (like lasers and radars) optimized by high-volume car manufacturing.

## Philosophy & Personal Leadership
* **Zen & The Power of Now:** Emphasizes a Zen Buddhist philosophy of focus—working entirely when working, sleeping entirely when sleeping, and letting go of failures immediately through extreme optimism.
* **Vision of Future Cities:** Envisions cities where autonomous fleets operate as coordinated systems rather than competing traffic, giving human freedom back by eliminating tedious two-hour commutes and transforming cars into moving living spaces.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Dr. Kai Yu predicts** all passenger vehicles in China will achieve 100% hands-free operation by the end of **2028**.
* **Dr. Kai Yu predicts** vehicles will achieve 100% eyes-off capability by the end of **2030**.
* **Dr. Kai Yu predicts** vehicles will achieve 100% minds-off capability (allowing sleeping while driving) by the end of **2035**.
* **Dr. Kai Yu predicts** meaningful volumes of humanoid robots will emerge for home service and elderly care within **5 years** (optimistic timeline).

## Notable Quotes
> "In some sense this is terrible business you know, heavy investment, very slow return, but in my view sometimes terrible business means a great business because that's the entry barrier for all the other newcomers is extremely high."
> — Dr. Kai Yu

> "The essence of robotics is to give the freedom, give the choice back to the human... In that [traffic] situation you are slave of the car because you don't have choice."
> — Dr. Kai Yu

> "When you are working you just focus on working. When you are sleeping just sleep, and then I focus the power of now."
> — Dr. Kai Yu

briefings.title: How Sam Altman Actually Uses AI to Run OpenAI and His Life
briefings.tldr: Sam Altman discusses how OpenAI's new "Dot" persistent agent protects his morning creative time, why developer demand for AI remains deeply human-centered, and how OpenAI is betting on a decentralized "Renaissance" for builders rather than a single corporate monopoly.
briefings.summary_markdown:
### TL;DR
Sam Altman discusses how OpenAI's new "Dot" persistent agent protects his morning creative time, why developer demand for AI remains deeply human-centered, and how OpenAI is betting on a decentralized "Renaissance" for builders rather than a single corporate monopoly.

## The Future of Engineering & Human-Centered AI
- **Latent Demand for Software:** Engineering coding models have not replaced developers; instead, they have unlocked massive latent demand. 
    - **Higher Bar:** Developers have never been able to do more, but society's expectations and the bar for quality have never been higher.
    - **Human-Centric Obsession:** Despite automation fears, public interest remains stubbornly focused on people, stories, and the human creators behind art and technology (e.g., the public reaction focusing on people involved rather than raw data center agent coordination).
- **Industrial Revolution vs. AI Renaissance:** Altman contrasts two opposing future models for AI:
    - **Industrial Revolution Model:** Treating humans as specialized cognitive cogs in a machine.
    - **Renaissance Model:** A massive expansion of human potential, scientific discovery, art, and one-person company formation where people regain control of their time.

## Protect Your Mornings: Sam Altman’s "Dot" Agent
- **Regaining Deep Work:** Altman’s new always-on agent, **"Dot"** (or "Dottie"), acts as a persistent triage system that protects his early morning window of maximum creativity by handling overnight fires and surfacing only truly urgent matters.
- **Proactive Context Synthesis:** 
    - **Cross-Platform Retrieval:** Dot successfully scanned images and Slack screenshots across systems to find a lost reference after Altman spent 10–20 minutes failing to locate it using Codex search.
    - **Live Iteration on Ideas:** Altman uses voice notes on walks or right before sleep to dump raw feature ideas; Dot then builds 5 or 6 versions for him to review and iterate on during spare moments.
- **Live Collaboration Spaces:** OpenAI built "Spaces" because traditional software abstractions break down when multiple people and multiple AI agents attempt to collaborate simultaneously on living documents and company dashboards that auto-update from Slack and real-world changes.

## Platform Ecosystem & Empowering Startups
- **Platform Strategy:** OpenAI explicitly rejects the philosophy that only one mega-corporation should exist; instead, they are betting heavily on an absolute lowering of the bar for one-person companies and small teams.
- **Bringing ChatGPT Subscriptions Everywhere:** OpenAI's new developer tools allow users to bring their ChatGPT subscriptions directly to third-party app developers and plugin extensions, eliminating the financial penalty of letting users run heavy AI models.
- **Startup Golden Age:** Altman notes that he has never seen startups get as successful as quickly, viewing the current ecosystem as an absolute golden age of entrepreneurship and creativity.

## Inference, Speed, and "Ultrafast" Prompting
- **The Ultrafast Workflow:** Altman conducts all of his prompting on **"Ultrafast"**, arguing that immediate connection and rapid feedback loops fundamentally transform a creator's iterative thinking process.
- **The Price of IQ vs. Speed:** OpenAI's historical focus has been driving down the price of intelligence; moving forward, speed and cost reduction will be pushed aggressively via custom chips and infrastructure investments to put high-speed inference into everyone's hands.

## Notable Quotes
> "People just want so much more stuff. People's expectations are so high. And I think that's a wonderful thing. I think this is why we will all have this incredible future in front of us to explore."
> — **Sam Altman**

> "One take on this would be that the Renaissance was fundamentally centered around people, and the industrial revolution was fundamentally centered around machines."
> — **Sam Altman**

> "We are not a gigantic company, first of all. Like, there's probably, I don't know, like maybe the big tech companies have like a hundred times more people than we do, something like that."
> — **Sam Altman**

briefings.title: Inside the Urgent Effort to Prepare America’s Workforce for a Massive AI Disruption
briefings.tldr: Former U.S. Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo leads the new organization RAISE US to prevent severe economic and gender inequality from AI disruption by partnering with state governors and business leaders on career transition pilots.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Former U.S. Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo leads the new organization RAISE US to prevent severe economic and gender inequality from AI disruption by partnering with state governors and business leaders on career transition pilots. Meanwhile, Maven CEO Kate Ryder emphasizes the enduring value of keeping healthcare human in an era of technological anxiety.

## Workforce Disruption & Economic Risks
- **Worst-Case Scenario:** Unchecked AI deployment could lead to tens of millions of displaced or underemployed workers, an unemployment rate of 10% to 20% among young people in their 20s, deep and long-term economic recession, street rioting, fraying democracy, and subsequent heavy regulation that halts innovation and cedes global leadership to China.
- **Vulnerable Job Categories:** Roles heavily clustered in clerical, administrative, and data tasks face immediate exposure, specifically call center workers, billing staff, claims assessors, healthcare coders, and researchers.
- **The Gender Gap Threat:** Raimondo expresses deep concern that AI will disproportionately impact women because they are clustered in vulnerable clerical/administrative roles and historically adopt new technology at slower rates than men.
- **Current Business Dynamics:** Corporate response is split; while some CEOs focus solely on short-term share price maximization, a coalition of 24 to 25 companies is partnering with RAISE US to proactively experiment with retraining and retention.

## RAISE US: Strategies & State-Level Pilots
- **Organizational Mission:** Serving as the leading organization to orchestrate a planned transition to an AI economy by providing private capital, partnering with governors, and redesigning workforce incentives.

- **Arkansas Partnership:** Working with the governor to embed navigation tools directly into unemployment insurance collection points to connect displaced workers with community skills training and open jobs.
- **Proposed Policy Levers:** Developing wage insurance pilots (such as in Pennsylvania) to top up salaries for older workers taking lower-paying transitional jobs, and reforming outdated unemployment insurance systems and payroll taxes that currently penalize human employment over AI agents.
- **Business Accelerators:** Operating small business accelerators to help individuals use AI to start their own businesses.

- **Advice for the Workforce:** Cultivate comfort with change, build continuous AI fluency rather than fear, and channel workplace anxiety into productive action and advocacy.
- **Enduring Human Capacities:** Judgment, reasoning, thinking, whole-context decision-making, and direct human-to-human interaction remain uniquely human and non-automated.
- **Alternative Sectors:** Non-college-educated individuals, particularly young women, are encouraged to consider high-demand, stable trades (such as plumbing, pipefitting, and electrical work) that require physical presence and are immune to AI automation.

## Healthcare & Human-Centric Care

* **Rise of the Attention Economy:** **Jake Paul** emphasizes that attention is one of the world's most valuable currencies, noting that traditional creators must transition into founders and operators to build enduring businesses.

* **Boxing & MMA Playbook:** **Jake Paul** transitioned into combat sports to maximize attention, staging massive events including a Netflix-streamed bout with Mike Tyson that drew 138 million viewers.
* **Challenging the UFC:** **Jake Paul** criticizes the UFC for paying fighters only ~15% of total revenue (compared to 50% in other major leagues) and launched MVP (Most Valuable Promotions), now managing 400 fighters and working to reform combat sports economics.
* **Women's Boxing Innovation:** **Jake Paul** highlights MVP's success in elevating women's boxing similar to the WNBA, providing young female fighters with higher pay and mainstream visibility.

## The Counter-Fund & Venture Investing
* **Angel Portfolio & Venture Fund:** **Jake Paul** started angel investing at age 18 in Silicon Valley, later launching a formal counter-fund with partner **Jeff Wu** that has backed companies like OpenAI (including co-creating the Sora social media app concept), Cognition, and SpaceX.
* **The "Celebrity VC" Stigma:** **Jake Paul** rejects the "celebrity investor" label, measuring his fund's performance and internal rate of return directly against traditional top-tier firms like Sequoia.
* **Multi-Pronged Strategy:** **Jake Paul** outlines a multi-stage venture approach spanning from seed-stage company building with founders to growth investments in top-tier teams.

## The Chainsmokers: From Music to Venture
* **Hype Machine Marketing:** **Alex Pall and Drew Taggart** describe how they built the Chainsmokers starting in 2012 by scouring Hype Machine blogs, analyzing student demographics, and sending personalized, witty emails to secure 30 number-one remixes in their first year.
* **The Music Industry Landscape:** **Drew Taggart** notes the extreme saturation of Spotify—with 300,000 tracks uploaded daily—and questions whether traditional label models are broken as artists increasingly seek direct audience ownership.
* **The "Sixth Man" VC Strategy:** **Alex Pall and Drew Taggart** run *Groove*, investing in cybersecurity, AI, infrastructure, deep tech, and health tech at the seed and Series A stages, positioning themselves not as lead VCs but as value-add marketing partners (comparing their role to NBA player Robert Horry).
* **The VC Reality Check:** **Drew Taggart** advises that venture capital requires 24/7 dedication, noting that the top 5% of investors capture 90% of returns, and that celebrity fame alone often brings fundraising skepticism from institutional LPs until consistent returns prove otherwise.

* **Underdog Fantasy & Dandy:** **Alex Pall and Drew Taggart** cite recent liquidity events like Underdog Fantasy (part of HG IG International) and portfolio company Dandy doubling annually as proof of disciplined venture execution.

briefings.title: Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari on the outlook, rates and monetary policy — 9/30/2026
briefings.tldr: Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari stated that inflation remains too high at around 3% and noted that the U.S. economy's resilience continues to surprise him, leading him to question how tight monetary policy actually is.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari stated that inflation remains too high at around 3% and noted that the U.S. economy's resilience continues to surprise him, leading him to question how tight monetary policy actually is. 

## Economic Outlook, Resilience, and Inflation
* **Inflation Status:** Kashkari stated that inflation is still too high, running at around a 3% rate and elevated for more than 5 years; the morning's PCE report did not change this fundamental story.
* **Consumer and Economic Resilience:** Consumer spending remains remarkably robust despite accumulated high prices over the past five plus years, supported by a low national unemployment rate of 4.1% and strong corporate profits across many sectors.
* **Supply Shock History:** Kashkari reflected on 5 years of rolling supply shocks (from COVID, Russia-Ukraine, trade wars/tariffs, and Middle East conflicts), noting that his initial "team transitory" stance was overwhelmed by persistent, rolling shocks that risk becoming embedded in economic decision-making.

## Monetary Policy, Neutral Rates, and Market Signals
* **Neutral Rate Adjustments:** Kashkari noted he has slowly revised up his estimate of the neutral federal funds rate, reaching 3.25% in September, but warned that the neutral rate may be temporarily elevated due to intense investment demand.
* **SEP Outlook (as of September):** Kashkari jotted down in pencil two hikes for the year (one already completed in September, with one more left), followed by another hike in 2027, though he emphasized this is subject to real-time adjustments based on new GDP revisions and consumer data.
* **Bond Market Divergence:** The 2-year Treasury yield ended around 4.88%, creating the largest gap ever recorded against the median implied 2-year rate from the dot plot (roughly 4.05%–4.06%), signaling to Kashkari that policy may need to go even tighter than expected.

## The AI Infrastructure Boom and Capital Allocation
* **Investment vs. Mortgage Rates:** Higher interest rates serve as the market mechanism to reallocate capital from housing and apartment construction toward building data centers, power, and water infrastructure for the AI buildout.
* **Efficiency and Resource Intensity:** Kashkari highlighted the massive resource intensity of AI (noting that creating a 6-second video using AI takes as much electricity as running a clothes dryer for an hour) and suggested that higher capital costs will force the industry to become much more efficient.
* **Productivity Paradox and Risks:** Kashkari is skeptical of Silicon Valley's hyper-optimistic growth claims (such as 10% real GDP growth), estimating that a realistic good scenario is raising productivity from 1.5% to 2%; a primary risk is that if the massive AI investment does not deliver expected productivity gains, it will result in "malinvestment" and an economic hangover.

## Federal Reserve Operations, Balance Sheet, and Governance
* **Balance Sheet Framework:** Kashkari views the $6.7 trillion balance sheet and swap lines as tools best reserved for zero-lower-bound crises or ensuring global dollar liquidity, while normal policy should rely on the federal funds rate.
* **IG Report Reaction:** Regarding the Federal Reserve Inspector General report finding management deficiencies and cost overruns in building renovations, Kashkari acknowledged it was a "bad look" and ironically noted that inflation itself was a major contributor to the cost overruns.
* **Fed Communication and Transparency:** Discussing Fed communication frameworks and task forces, Kashkari emphasized that his goal in speaking publicly is to share his personal reaction function and the specific data elements he monitors to help market participants.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* *No genuine forward-looking claims containing concrete targets, timelines, or quantitative predictions about future events were made by the speaker in this transcript (projections such as rate hikes were explicitly framed as conditional snapshots based on meeting-day data rather than concrete forward bets).*

## Notable Quotes
* > "My basic takeaway on the inflation data is that inflation is still too high. It's running... at around a 3% rate. Uh it's been elevated now for more than 5 years." — Neel Kashkari
* > "The longer this goes on, the longer the economy is proving to be resilient in the face of all these shocks, the more I am questioning how tight is monetary policy." — Neel Kashkari
* > "If you'd asked me in my first five years, would we ever endure five years of elevated inflation? I would have said, 'Not a chance. There's no way that could happen.' And yet here we are." — Neel Kashkari

AI co-founder Greg Brockman predicts a massive renaissance of entrepreneurship over the next 1-2 years driven by accessible intelligence, while host Silicon Valley Girl explores how small businesses and creators can leverage AI agents to scale beyond traditional limitations.

- **Proactive AI Assistants:** Current AI models are moving beyond passive chat to proactive assistance, such as drafting responses to neglected emails or managing calendars autonomously.

briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Pershing Square founder and CEO Bill Ackman discussed his strategy for Howard Hughes Corp., the capitalization of insurance venture Vantage, Pershing Square USA's market discount, AI frontier models, and a new brain-care institute inspired by his daughter's recovery.

## Howard Hughes & Vantage Insurance Strategy
* **Taking a Page from Buffett:** Pershing Square is replicating Berkshire Hathaway's playbook by utilizing Vantage—a specialty insurer and reinsurer closed in June—as a cash-flow-generating vehicle with low leverage.
* **Leadership & Asset Allocation:** Mark Risan (former CEO of Arch Capital Group) serves as executive chair of Vantage, alongside David Gansburg and Lucy Vetto. 
* **Treasury & Equity Split:** Fixed income assets were immediately sold upon closing; approximately 65% of Vantage assets are in short-term treasuries and 35% in a managed common stock portfolio, with common stock exposure ultimately targeted at 40% to 45%.
* **Howard Hughes Real Estate Restructuring:** 
  * Howard Hughes is shifting from 100% equity financing to bringing in third-party partners (such as Brookfield or Blackstone) to reduce equity commitment in real estate by up to 80%.
  * The restructuring aims to free up **$2 billion to $3 billion** in equity by the end of next year to redeploy into Vantage.

## Pershing Square USA (PSUS) & Market Dynamics
* **Fund Structure & Cost:** PSUS is a liquid public closed-end fund charging no incentive fee, offering retail investors access to Pershing Square's strategy at the lowest cost globally.
* **Performance & Deployment:** Net Asset Value (NAV) is down about 3% from the IPO (with ~240 basis points driven by IPO costs); capital has been fully deployed into "super durable growth companies."
* **Discount and Valuation Realities:** PSUS shares trade at a 25% discount to NAV; Ackman attributes this to a marketing and awareness challenge rather than underlying portfolio weakness, pointing to discounted entry prices on holdings like Meta, S&P Global (bought at 21x earnings vs. typical 30x), and Intercontinental Exchange (bought at 17x vs. 24x).

## AI, Frontier Models, and IPOs
* **Anthropic and OpenAI:** Ackman praised Anthropic's rapid revenue ramp and product quality (noting internal use of Claude), questioning whether frontier model companies can maintain market presence against open-source and open-weight models.
* **Capital Intensity vs. Durability:** Pershing Square avoids fast-growing, capital-consuming AI companies where investors bet on future line crossings, preferring predictable businesses like Microsoft, Visa, and Mastercard.
* **Catastrophic Risk & Regulation:** Ackman is less concerned about regulated labs like Anthropic or OpenAI causing systemic harm—arguing that massive financial and legal disincentives provide self-regulation—and more concerned about rogue actors exploiting open-source models without guardrails.

## Medical Innovation & New Brain Institute
* **Daughter Lucy’s Recovery:** Ackman detailed the severe brain hemorrhage suffered by his daughter Lucy, who lost the ability to speak, walk, and see light, but is making progress through aggressive care, nutrition, and experimental mitochondrial therapy (which restored light perception to 22,000 in one eye).
* **New Brain Institute:** Inspired by Lucy's journey, Ackman and his wife are building a new institute focused on delivering direct clinical care, leveraging data generated by emerging brain-interface technologies (such as Neuralink, Precision Neuroscience, and Synchron) combined with AI data-processing capabilities.

## Notable Quotes
> "The combination of growing a very valuable business inside a company and not issuing stock as you grow led to enormous per share value being created. Basically we're taking a page from Mr. Buffett."
> — Bill Ackman

> "I can't tell you where any stock we own is going to trade in the next 90 days. We own businesses based on how we expect them the returns we generate over the next 5 years not 5 minutes not next 90 days."
> — Bill Ackman

> "I'm actually less concerned about anthropic or open AI being the source of the problem. I'm probably maybe more concerned about a bad actor, a rogue actor who does not have the same considerations, who uses the resources of an open source model to cause enormous harm."
> — Bill Ackman

briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth delivered the 2026 State of the Force Address at Marine Corps Base Quantico, declaring a permanent shift toward a merit-based, warfighting-focused culture and announcing six major structural initiatives spanning autonomous warfare, future strategy, domestic resilience, a new military base, academic commissioning pipelines, and spiritual support.

## Cultural Transformation & Leadership
* **Revival of the Warrior Ethos:** **Cultural Reset:** The Department of War has replaced social engineering, diversity quotas, and risk aversion with a focus on training, readiness, accountability, discipline, and lethality.
* **Personnel and Standards:** **Merit-Based Standards:** The department has eliminated DEI evaluations (such as B-Cap and C-Cap) and established gender-neutral standards across all combat MOS roles set exclusively to the highest male standard.
* **General Officer Accountability:** **10% Reduction:** The department has fired 10% of generals and admirals and reduced overall general officer slots by an additional 10% (a total 20% reduction across the board).
* **Retention and Recruitment:** **Record Metrics:** Retention rates are at historic highs (including over 80% on the USS *Abraham Lincoln*), and recruiting across all branches has reached decades-long highs following the November 2024 election.

## Six Strategic Announcements
* **Autonomous Warfare Command (Auto-Warcom):** **Four-Star Command:** Creation of a new four-star combatant command with service-like authorities to scale autonomous and robotic capabilities rapidly across the joint force.
  * **Project Agincourt:** An interim step replacing the Unmanned Systems Derpom within the DIU to prototype "warfighting acquisition," fusing operators with entrepreneurs in rapid adaptation cycles.
  * **Leadership Appointments:** Owen West and Navy SEAL Senior Chief Max Strazer appointed to a CEO-COO partnership to guide Project Agincourt over the next year.
* **Project Meridian:** **Future of Warfare Study:** An initiative led by CTO Emil Michael and co-led by Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey, and Newt Gingrich, alongside private-sector and academic experts, tasked with mapping war's domains and technologies over the next 120 days.
* **Fortress America (Federal Operations for Resilience, Troop Resources, Energy, Supply, and Survivability):** **National Insurance Policy:** A directive requiring every major U.S. military installation to generate its own power independent of the civilian grid, bringing critical supply chains (rare earths, semiconductors, propellants) home, and building deep strategic reserves for munitions, fuel, medicine, and blood.
* **The Next Great American Base:** **First New Base in 40 Years:** A call to governors and Adjutant Generals (TAGs) to pitch state sites to host 15,000 to 25,000 troops on hundreds of thousands of acres featuring classical architecture, modern air defenses, and organic power generation.
* **America's Corps of Cadets:** **New Academic Pipelines:** Partnering with premier higher education institutions—specifically Louisiana State University (LSU), Liberty University, Tuskegee University, Mississippi State University, and Hillsdale College—to establish new corps of cadets, designated as distinguished military colleges with priority in officer commissioning.
* **Office of Religious Affairs:** **Direct Reporting:** Establishment of a direct-line Office of Religious Affairs reporting straight to the Secretary of War to protect chaplain budgets, infrastructure, and spiritual support for a force where less than 5% identify as non-religious.

## Operations & Theater Updates
* **Counter-Cartel Operations:** **A-Triple-C:** The Counter-Cartel Coalition has put regional terrorist organizations and cartels on the run in the Western Hemisphere.
* **Middle East Campaigns:** **Iran Neutralization:** U.S. forces operating under clear authorities have dismantled Iran's navy, air force, air defense systems, leadership, and military-industrial base, ensuring Iran will not attain a nuclear weapon.

## Notable Quotes
> "Instead, the speech was a declaration of independence for the War Department, marking a clean break from the Defense Department of old. The speech reestablished a singular mission for this department: warfighting. Preparing to fight and preparing to win. Unrelenting, unapologetic, and uncompromising in that single pursuit."
> — Secretary of War Pete Hegseth

> "We are no longer the woke department or the weak department. Simple translation of that, no fanny no fatties, no trannies, no beardos, no weirdos, no wimps, no radicals, just warriors."
> — Secretary of War Pete Hegseth

> "You see the Ivy League faculty lounges, they'll never understand you, and that's okay, because they could never, ever do what you do. The media will mischaracterize you, and that's okay, because deep down, they know you're the reason they live free."
> — Secretary of War Pete Hegseth

briefings.title: The $500B Opportunity in Europe’s Defense Buildout
briefings.tldr: Europe is mobilizing up to €800B in defense spending, but the real bottleneck is manufacturing at scale rather than inventing new technology; modern warfare requires components produced in the tens of thousands or millions, creating a massive opportunity for industrial consolidation and supply chain innovation.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Europe is mobilizing up to €800B in defense spending, but the real bottleneck is manufacturing at scale rather than inventing new technology; modern warfare requires components produced in the tens of thousands or millions, creating a massive opportunity for industrial consolidation and supply chain innovation.

## The State of European Defense & Lessons from Ukraine
* **Underinvestment and Exposure:** 
  * Europe underinvested in defense for decades before the Russia-Ukraine war exposed severe weaknesses in manufacturing capacity and scale-supply.
  * **Aistis Šimaitis (Onodrim):** Noted that the war proved "volume wins," shifting defense priorities from exquisite, unmassable technologies to systems that can be produced in tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands, or millions.
  * **George Hadjiminas (Theon International):** Added that many U.S.-deployed systems initially failed in Ukraine and required iterative testing cycles before working properly in the field.
* **Procurement and Market Fragmentation:**
  * **George Hadjiminas:** Pointed out that Europe has too many national champions protected by individual countries with conflicting interests, unlike the consolidated U.S. market.
  * **Aistis Šimaitis:** Noted that European defense procurement is fragmented country-by-country, and existing military-industrial complexes rely on outdated supply chains where countries like Germany hold large volumes of non-working systems.

## Manufacturing Gaps & The Scale Paradigm
* **Component Lead Times and White Space:**
  * **Bruno Wejchert (Strike Capital):** Highlighted that component lead times can stretch into years, causing certain primes to take 4 to 5 years to deliver on contracts.
  * Identified the primary white space as the manufacturing gap for supplying next-generation primes built on outdated supply chains.
* **Autonomous Warfare Economics:**
  * **Aistis Šimaitis:** Stated that autonomous mass tech requires formerly expensive components (like $30,000 radios or cameras) to become significantly cheaper and produced at much higher scale.
* **Onodrim's Acquisition Strategy:**
  * **Aistis Šimaitis:** Explained that Onodrim acquires high-quality manufacturing and critical mission system businesses in Europe to ensure defense primes can deliver orders over the next decade without being a bottleneck.
* **Theon International's Position:**
  * **George Hadjiminas:** Noted that Theon focuses on electrooptics (night vision, AR head-up displays) and leveraged the defense boom through a 2024 IPO and strong growth trajectory.

## Technology vs. Industrial Execution in Defense
* **The Winning Recipe for Defense Companies:**
  * **George Hadjiminas:** Argued that prototypes don't fight wars, and success requires a combination of technological forefront development and industrial acuity to deliver at scale; it is an evolution rather than a revolution.
  * **Aistis Šimaitis:** Offered a controversial take that tech companies (doing AI/software/final assembly) should *not* want to be manufacturing giants; instead, they should partner in a non-zero-sum way with industrial component-producing companies.
* **Venture Capital Realities & Defense Bubbles:**
  * **Bruno Wejchert:** Warned that many European startups funded with minimal capital ($5M–$10M) struggle because governments lack belief in small balance sheets; however, de facto category kings like Helsing (Germany) and satellite-aperture radar firms are eating away traditional prime market share.

## Talent & Funding Dynamics
* **Hiring and Talent Influx:**
  * **Aistis Šimaitis:** Stated that hiring into defense has been great due to Europe's re-industrialization ambition; cited his co-founder/CTO (Alex) moving back to Germany from the US after 17 years. Companies like Helsing also experience zero talent attraction problems.
* **Funding Mechanisms:**
  * **Aistis Šimaitis:** Explained that government is the primary buyer (backed by EU initiatives and trillion-dollar funding targets by 2030), which in turn triggers venture and private funding.

## Notable Quotes
> *"You'd rather have a million of something and one of anything."* — **Aistis Šimaitis**

> *"Prototypes don't fight wars no matter how good they are. They cannot win wars."* — **George Hadjiminas**

> *"Focus on being important and valuable and the money will come."* — **Aistis Šimaitis** (recalling a lesson learned from Palantir's Alex Karp)

briefings.title: Watch CNBC's interview with Citadel's Ken Griffin and Carnegie Mellon Univ. Pres. Farnam Jahanian
briefings.tldr: Citadel CEO Ken Griffin announced a historic $3 billion investment in Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) alongside President Farnam Jahanian, aimed at reshaping higher education and establishing a new integrated campus model in Miami focused on societal grand challenges.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Citadel CEO Ken Griffin announced a historic $3 billion investment in Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) alongside President Farnam Jahanian, aimed at reshaping higher education and establishing a new integrated campus model in Miami focused on societal grand challenges. 

## The $3 Billion CMU Investment & New Higher Ed Model
- **Historic Gift:** Ken Griffin announced a $3 billion investment in Carnegie Mellon University, developed over 2.5 to 3 years.
- **Campus Distribution:** The funds will support CMU's Pittsburgh campus and build a new, fully integrated campus in Miami.
- **Interdisciplinary Educational Model (President Farnam Jahanian):** 
  - Moves away from traditional departments, colleges, and majors.
  - **Societal Grand Challenges Focus:** Organizes the Miami campus around areas like human health, national security, economic competitiveness, cybersecurity, energy/climate resiliency, and advanced manufacturing/re-industrialization.
- **Institutional Alignment (Ken Griffin):** 
  - Chosen due to CMU's willingness to think creatively and step out of the box.
  - Ranked #1 nationally in computer science, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and world-renowned in robotics, alongside a strong fine arts/drama program (including the first degree-granting drama program in 1914, producing nearly 70 Tony Award winners).

## Higher Education, Return on Investment, and Economic Literacy
- **Ranking Improvements (President Farnam Jahanian):** 
  - CMU's national US News & World Report undergraduate ranking rose from #20 to #14 in one year.
  - **ROI Metrics:** CMU is in the top three nationally for graduate return on investment.
- **Holistic Skill Development:** Emphasizes teaching critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and communication alongside science and technology, maintaining high standards without grade inflation.
- **Critique of Economic Ideologies (Ken Griffin):** 
  - Expressed concern over rising socialism among young graduates, attributing it to "economic illiteracy."
  - Argued that higher education must return to academic rigor, common sense, and basic principles, noting historical failures of socialism (e.g., China).

## Market Events & AI Concentration
- **Situational Awareness Liquidation Event (Ken Griffin):** 
  - Explained behind-the-scenes actions regarding Situational Awareness, an AI-focused fund that faced valuation setbacks due to too much leverage and enthusiasm.
  - **Citadel's Rescue:** Citadel spent roughly 40 hours straight working on the liquidity challenges and bought most of the fund's portfolio to resolve issues for limited partners and Citadel fund investors.
- **National Debt & Productivity:** Stated that America's $40 trillion national debt requires economic growth driven by productivity, with AI, robotics, and computer science serving as vital tools.
- **AI Dualism & Guardrails (President Farnam Jahanian):** 
  - Students are finding strong employment and are not worried about job prospects.
  - Emphasized approaching AI with wide eyes, balancing technological advances (personalized therapeutics, infrastructure protection) with ethical implications, policy considerations, and regulatory frameworks.

## Talent, Hiring, and Regional Transformation
- **Hiring Criteria at Citadel (Ken Griffin):** Looks for candidates with serious educational backgrounds, grit, determination, work ethic, and a passion for lifetime learning.
- **Talent Demand:** Candidates with backgrounds in AI and computer science are the most sought-after and difficult to recruit in current job markets.
- **Urban Transformation (Ken Griffin):** 
  - Great universities anchor great cities.
  - Bringing CMU to Miami will be "transitive" for Miami, much like CMU has been transformative for Pittsburgh—which is currently surrounded by around 100 robotics companies driving the re-industrialization of America.

## Notable Quotes
> "This is a $3 billion investment in Carnegie Melon. It's an investment in excellence in higher education in America... Carnegie Melon is number one in the nation in computer science, artificial intelligence, cyber security, worldrenowned program in robotics..."
> — Ken Griffin

> "The model essentially moves away from thinking about universities in the context of departments, colleges and majors. Instead, we focus and organize the campus around societal grand challenge areas such as human health, national security, our economic competitiveness..."
> — President Farnam Jahanian

> "There is no point in the history of humanity where socialism has worked. I mean look at the great experiment in China. 50 million people died of starvation. Why do we think this is worthy to teach in our classes in our universities?"
> — Ken Griffin

briefings.title: We’re Reaching the Physical Limits of Chips
briefings.tldr: Memory prices have surged 700% this year amid severe physical limits in semiconductor manufacturing, driving an urgent hardware renaissance where power, cooling, and data transfer bottlenecks are reshaping the AI infrastructure stack.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Memory prices have surged 700% this year amid severe physical limits in semiconductor manufacturing, driving an urgent hardware renaissance where power, cooling, and data transfer bottlenecks are reshaping the AI infrastructure stack.

## Semiconductor Physics and Manufacturing Constraints
* **Moore's Law Plateau:** **Steven Latré** notes that transistor scaling has reached physical limits, with depths now at roughly 1 nanometer (100,000 times smaller than a human hair), requiring significantly more inventive hardware approaches.
* **The Imec Role:** **Steven Latré** describes imec as a 40-year-old Belgian R&D leader operating a unique clean room facility where almost every major chip in the world is designed 5 to 10 years ahead of commercialization.
* **Chip Design Diversification:** **Steven Latré** states that endless market demand for custom silicon is driving the creation of new chip companies, requiring hardware diversification beyond standard GPUs to match emerging software algorithms.

## Infrastructure Bottlenecks: Memory, Power, and Cooling
* **Memory Shortage & Price Spikes:** **Adam Chambers** identifies memory bandwidth and latency as the primary constraint at the inference layer; **Steven Latré** notes memory is already "broken today." 
    * **Market Concentration:** **Adam Chambers** points out that 95% of memory production is controlled by just three companies (Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung), with two based in Korea.
    * **Hyperscaler Impact:** **Adam Chambers** notes that hyperscalers have absorbed entire inventory supplies, causing memory prices to rise by **700%** this year.
* **Power and Cooling Challenges:** **Adam Chambers** highlights power constraints as a massive bottleneck and predicts that liquid cooling will progress over the next 5 to 10 years by moving physically closer and closer to the GPU itself.

## The Software-Hardware Paradigm Shift
* **Value Reversal:** **Adam Chambers** references discussions with Tony Kim of BlackRock at the Raise AI Summit in Paris, noting a hardware renaissance where chip margins are fantastic while software faces compression.
* **Software Immaturity:** **Steven Latré** argues the shift isn't a permanent flip of the pyramid, but rather reflects the immaturity of current AI software, which relies on a "brute force approach" that will eventually evolve to integrate more closely with hardware.
* **Model Size Limits:** **Steven Latré** asserts that building ever-larger models will stop, noting that open-source models like **K3D** already exceed the human brain's parameters while remaining about a million times less energy efficient.

## Photonics as the Next-Generation Interconnect
* **Overcoming Copper Limitations:** **Adam Chambers** and **Steven Latré** agree that copper wiring has reached its limits due to latent heat and electrical inefficiencies.
* **Photonics Advantages:** **Adam Chambers** explains that using light instead of electrons attacks multiple bottlenecks simultaneously by increasing transfer speeds, reducing cooling requirements, and improving core data transfer efficiency.
* **Evolution of Optical Architecture:** **Adam Chambers** predicts that over the next 5 years, optical components will move closer to the GPU, shifting from linear pluggable optics between clusters to co-packaged optics.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Steven Latré** predicts that in 5 to 10 years, people will laugh at today's AI and view large language models' brute-force approach the same way people now view dial-up internet connections.
* **Adam Chambers** predicts that over the next 5 to 10 years, liquid cooling will progress by bringing cooling liquid closer and closer to the actual GPU.
* **Adam Chambers** predicts that within the next 5 years, optical components will move closer to the GPU toward a state of co-packaged optics.

## Notable Quotes
> "There's almost no chip in the world today that has not been touched by imec in some way."
> — **Steven Latré**

> "We went from 175 billion parameters to kind of 10 trillion parameters right right now. That's going to stop."
> — **Steven Latré**

> "I think five to 10 years from now we're going to laugh at how old-fashioned AI was today."
> — **Steven Latré**
